title: Session endpoints: GET /me and PUT /me/preferences
objective: Port the session bootstrap surface: GET /me (identity, tenant memberships, active/last tenant, effective permissions for the active tenant, theme) and PUT /me/preferences (last tenant + theme persistence), byte-compatible with the existing DTOs so the SPA shell works unchanged (P-01, section 12 session/platform).
scope: GET /api/v1/me: authenticated, returns the reference DTO — user identity (first/last/email), isInternal/global capabilities, tenant memberships (active tenants only), lastTenantId, theme, effective permissions for the resolved tenant context per the reference contract
PUT /api/v1/me/preferences: persists last active tenant and theme; validates tenant membership before accepting lastTenantId
Zero-membership Internal users: /me must succeed and expose global permissions so the shell can operate (prior-build T-045 parity)
implementation_details: Verify exact DTO field names against the .NET Me endpoint and the SPA's Redux session slice — contract preservation is the acceptance bar (A-3).
Effective permissions computed via the T-012 module for the active tenant (or global-only for zero-membership Internal users).
PUT /me/preferences validates theme against the allowed set and lastTenantId against the caller's memberships (or Internal grant); rejects removed tenants.
No X-Tenant-Id requirement on /me itself if the reference treats it as global — mirror the reference routing classification.

unit: None beyond schema edge cases (covered at integration)
integration: Seeded multi-tenant user: /me returns memberships, last tenant, theme, effective permissions matching fixtures
Preferences roundtrip: PUT then GET reflects changes; invalid theme 422; non-member lastTenantId rejected
Zero-membership Internal user gets a working /me with global permissions

history.message: Task generated by Planner from approved spec.md. Maps to P-01, A-3 contract, section 12 session/platform.

Delegated to Implementor. T-015 and T-016 run in parallel (domains/session vs domains/tenants). T-014 (RLS) deliberately deferred to run ALONE afterwards: it changes the app DB role and adds SET LOCAL context to the data path, which could destabilise every integration suite, so it should not compete with concurrent test runs. Orchestrator owns harness JSON.

GET /me + PUT /me/preferences implemented, byte-compatible with the .NET DTOs. MEASURED with citations: GetMeResult (GetMeQuery.cs:26-34), MembershipDto (:41-46), camelCase via System.Text.Json; per-membership permission resolution + ordinal sort (GetMeQueryHandler.cs:53-62,74); left-joined currency with BWP/BWP fallback and order by t.Name (UserTenantMembershipReader.cs:39-50); NULL FIELD = LEAVE ALONE, NOT CLEAR (UserPreferencesStore.cs:27-35); lastTenantId validated via the shared ITenantAccessValidator (SetMePreferencesCommandHandler.cs:70); 401/403/422 and Results.Ok() = 200 with an EMPTY BODY (MeEndpoints.cs:28-52); theme allow-list ['light','dark'] with its exact message (SetMePreferencesValidator.cs:14,21). userId/tenantId are JSON NUMBERS, deliberately not the repo's bigint-as-string convention, because src/ui/src/api/me.ts:9,18 declares number and AuthProvider.tsx:26 compares with ===. FOUR REFERENCE-vs-SPA DISAGREEMENTS REPORTED RATHER THAN SILENTLY PICKED: (1) wire name is effectivePermissions; the Redux slice's `permissions` is a client-side rename in AuthProvider.tsx:96 - emits the wire name and asserts the payload does NOT carry `permissions`. (2) The brief said permissions are 'for the active tenant' but the reference returns a set PER MEMBERSHIP with the SPA selecting client-side (sessionSlice.ts:145-149) - followed the reference; the active tenant's set is still correct. (3) DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE: the reference had exactly one HasQueryFilter (QuoteIqDbContext.cs:580, tenant scoping), so its inner join returned SOFT-REMOVED tenants in /me and TenantAccessValidator then 403'd every request made in them - a real reference bug; AC-025/AC-027/V-032 require exclusion, so this port filters tenants.status='active' and also refuses a removed tenant as lastTenantId even for a member. (4) Minor: reference /me problems use title 'Request failed' while T-009's mapper derives title from status; harmless since the SPA renders detail ?? title and detail is always populated. ZERO-MEMBERSHIP INTERNAL USERS: no bail-out path; memberships comes back [] and globalPermissions carries tenant-less grants resolved at tenantId null. PUT /me/preferences reuses T-013's createTenantAccessValidator rather than a second hand-written membership lookup, so 'may I persist tenant X' and 'may I enter tenant X' cannot drift apart. 7 mutants all killed, with four named positive controls so the negatives cannot be satisfied by a reject-everything handler (happy-path DTO; both allowed themes accepted; empty globalPermissions for a tenant-only member, which stops the global-union test being vacuous; Internal holder CAN persist a non-member tenant, which stops the 403 tests passing via a bare membership check). Gates: typecheck 0, lint 0, 53 files / 838 tests / 0 skipped, ci:test 0 with the floor raised 808 -> 838. FLAGGED FOR EVALUATOR: no audit row is written for preference changes - the reference does not audit /me either, but CLAUDE.md asks for auditability of tenant-scoped changes and a tenant switch is arguably one; implementor flagged rather than deciding. E2E V-033/V-044 not done - jointly owned with T-018/T-043, target e2e_tests/tests/shell.spec.ts, and depend on the SPA actually calling this API, which it does not yet; the server-side halves are proven at integration level.

Evaluator PASS at iteration 0. GATES RE-RUN WITH DIRECTLY CAPTURED EXIT CODES: npm test 55 files / 873 passed / 0 skipped exit 0; ci:test exit 0 (873 >= floor 873, 0 skipped); typecheck 0; lint 0; db:validate 0 (22 migrations from empty twice, identical schema, snapshot match). RULING 1 (removed-tenant divergence) - DIVERGENCE CORRECT: evaluator independently confirmed the reference defect (UserTenantMembershipReader.cs joins Tenants with NO status predicate; the sole HasQueryFilter at QuoteIqDbContext.cs:580 is tenant-scoping, not soft-delete; TenantAccessValidator.cs returns TenantNotActive for Status != Active - so /me listed removed tenants the validator then 403'd). AC-025 ('excluding removed tenants'), AC-027, and V-032's negative test explicitly mandate exclusion; a faithful port would violate approved acceptance criteria. Note: refusing a removed lastTenantId is NOT a divergence at all - the reference's SetMePreferencesCommandHandler.cs:67-73 already used the shared ITenantAccessValidator whose status check refuses it; the only true divergence is the /me membership filter. RULING 2 (per-membership permissions) - IMPLEMENTOR RIGHT TO FOLLOW THE REFERENCE: GetMeQueryHandler.cs:51-62 resolves a set PER MEMBERSHIP; MembershipDto carries EffectivePermissions; the SPA consumes exactly that (me.ts declares effectivePermissions per membership; AuthProvider maps m.effectivePermissions -> permissions; sessionSlice selectHasPermission picks the ACTIVE tenant's set client-side). Returning one active-tenant set would leave the switcher unable to gate nav for other tenants without a round trip - a contract break. RULING 3 (preference audit) - NOT REQUIRED NOW, recorded as a note: AC-024's operation inventory (the approved audit bar) does not include preference changes or tenant switches; V-031 likewise; the reference does not audit /me; last_tenant_id/theme_preference are user-scoped profile fields, not tenant-scoped business data; the security-relevant event (an Internal user actually ENTERING another tenant) is already audited by T-013 per AC-020 at first use. If the human wants switch-persistence audited it is a spec/acceptance amendment, not a T-015 defect. EVALUATOR-RUN MUTANTS (both killed, restores verified sha256-identical): (1) dropped the tenants.status='active' predicate -> 2 targeted failures (the exclusion test and the membership-count test); (2) reject-every-lastTenantId handler -> 6 failures including the named Internal-holder positive control, proving the 403 negatives cannot be satisfied vacuously. Byte-compat spot-checked first-hand against the reference and SPA: field set/casing, numbers-not-strings ids, effectivePermissions wire name (+ explicit not-permissions assertion), null-present-not-absent, BWP/BWP left-join fallback, ordinal sort, order by tenant name, 401/403/422, Results.Ok() = 200 EMPTY body, null-means-leave-alone, theme allow-list with the verbatim message. Cross-user isolation verified (user_id predicate + dedicated test; callerUserId only from the verified principal). KNOWN LIMITS recorded, not credited: V-033/V-044 e2e deferred to T-018/T-043 (SPA does not call this API yet); no real CI run; Node 22 unexercised.
